dark age.title: Dark Age
dark age.author: Pierce Brown
dark age.why: Fourth Red Rising book of relentless space war and politics; readers find it impossible to put down.

charlottes web.title: Charlotte's Web
charlottes web.author: E. B. White
charlottes web.why: A pig is saved by a spider's words; a children's classic readers remember for its famous opening line and gentle wisdom.

trout fishing in america.title: Trout Fishing in America
trout fishing in america.author: Richard Brautigan
trout fishing in america.why: Quirky, surreal sketches of America built around trout fishing; loved for its odd, memorable lines.

crow road.title: The Crow Road
crow road.author: Iain Banks
crow road.why: A Scottish family saga and mystery that opens with a famously striking first line; readers cherish Banks's mix of humour and darkness.

pines.title: Pines
pines.author: Blake Crouch
pines.why: A federal agent wakes in a strange idyllic town he cannot leave; a gripping mystery with a big reveal, though a few readers disliked it.

candy house.title: The Candy House
candy house.author: Jennifer Egan
candy house.why: Interlinked stories about a device that uploads memory; inventive and sharp, praised as stunningly good.

homecoming.title: Homecoming
homecoming.author: Kate Morton
homecoming.why: Comments mention several unrelated Homecoming books; no clear recommendation.

talented mr ripley.title: The Talented Mr. Ripley
talented mr ripley.author: Patricia Highsmith
talented mr ripley.why: A charming con man slides into murder and identity theft in Italy; a suspense classic recommended for its chilling protagonist.

thud.title: Thud!
thud.author: Terry Pratchett
thud.why: Commander Vimes confronts a dwarf-troll tension in Ankh-Morpork; a fan-favourite Discworld Watch story.

horns.title: Horns
horns.author: Joe Hill
horns.why: A man wakes with horns and the power to hear people's sins while hunting his girlfriend's killer; readers say it beats the film.

border trilogy.title: The Border Trilogy (All the Pretty Horses / The Crossing / Cities of the Plain)
border trilogy.author: Cormac McCarthy
border trilogy.why: Cormac McCarthy's three linked novels of cowboys in the borderlands; a recommended masterpiece for fans of Western epics.

angels.title: Angels
angels.author: Denis Johnson
angels.why: Denis Johnson's raw debut about drifters on a doomed road trip; readers say it stuck with them.

final empire.title: The Final Empire
final empire.author: Brandon Sanderson
final empire.why: A thief crew plots to topple an immortal ruler in a world of ash; a gripping, hard-to-put-down start to Mistborn.

time enough for love.title: Time Enough For Love
time enough for love.author: Robert A. Heinlein
time enough for love.why: The oldest man alive reflects on his many lives; readers say it changed their sense of what matters.

oliver twist.title: Oliver Twist
oliver twist.author: Charles Dickens
oliver twist.why: An orphan falls among London thieves; Dickens's classic about poverty and kindness, liked by readers who enjoy his style.

priestdaddy.title: Priestdaddy
priestdaddy.author: Patricia Lockwood
priestdaddy.why: A poet's memoir about living with her eccentric Catholic priest father; praised as hilarious and beautifully written.

plague dogs.title: The Plague Dogs
plague dogs.author: Richard Adams
plague dogs.why: Two dogs escape a laboratory and struggle to survive; an uncomfortable but gripping story that readers say is well worth it.

penance.title: Penance
penance.author: Eliza Clark
penance.why: A true-crime writer reconstructs a teen murder through interviews; compelling and addictive, with sharp 2000s culture.

ship who sang.title: The Ship Who Sang
ship who sang.author: Anne McCaffrey
ship who sang.why: A woman housed in a starship's shell works as its brain; a classic about humanity and technology.

steerswoman.title: The Steerswoman
steerswoman.author: Rosemary Kirstein
steerswoman.why: A woman who gathers knowledge uncovers a mystery in a world that hides science; an underrated science-fantasy gem.

summer.title: Summer
summer.author: Edith Wharton
summer.why: A young woman in a New England village falls into a doomed romance; praised as piercing and beautiful.

nights dawn trilogy.title: The Night's Dawn Trilogy
nights dawn trilogy.author: Peter F. Hamilton
nights dawn trilogy.why: A huge space opera in which the dead return; a sprawling beast of a story some call so bad it is good.

firefly.title: Firefly
firefly.author: Piers Anthony
firefly.why: Named only to warn readers away because of disturbing content.

king rat.title: King Rat
king rat.author: James Clavell
king rat.why: Prisoners of war struggle to survive in a Japanese camp; recommended as gripping.

friday.title: Friday
friday.author: Robert A. Heinlein
friday.why: Comments refer to other books titled Friday; no clear recommendation.

shards of earth.title: Shards of Earth
shards of earth.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
shards of earth.why: Humans and alien species fight cosmic threats in a Mass Effect-style space opera; good from start to finish.

final girl support group.title: The Final Girl Support Group
final girl support group.author: Grady Hendrix
final girl support group.why: Slasher survivors in therapy are hunted again; a clever, fast horror-comedy readers enjoy.

sandman.title: Sandman
sandman.author: Neil Gaiman
sandman.why: Neil Gaiman's dark fantasy comic about the lord of dreams; readers call it a masterpiece.

slow horses.title: Slow Horses
slow horses.author: Mick Herron
slow horses.why: Disgraced spies exiled to a dead-end department stumble on a plot; sharp, witty spy fiction.

secret life of bees.title: The secret life of bees
secret life of bees.author: Sue Monk Kidd
secret life of bees.why: A girl runs away to a house of beekeeping sisters in 1960s South Carolina; a warm, popular coming-of-age story.

bear and the nightingale.title: The Bear and the Nightingale
bear and the nightingale.author: Katherine Arden
bear and the nightingale.why: A girl guards her family against old spirits in medieval Russia; atmospheric folklore fantasy.

legendborn.title: Legendborn
legendborn.author: Tracy Deonn
legendborn.why: A grieving student discovers a secret society descended from Arthurian knights; an absorbing YA fantasy.

dead wake.title: Dead Wake
dead wake.author: Erik Larson
dead wake.why: The sinking of the Lusitania told like a thriller; readers enjoy the fascinating detail.

slow gods.title: Slow Gods
slow gods.author: Claire North
slow gods.why: A space opera of long journeys and slow time; liked for feeling fresh.

grendel.title: Grendel
grendel.author: John Gardner
grendel.why: Beowulf's monster narrates his own story; readers reread it for its sublime prose.

winter of our discontent.title: The Winter of Our Discontent
winter of our discontent.author: John Steinbeck
winter of our discontent.why: A decent man in a small town is tempted into compromising his morals; a late Steinbeck about ambition and integrity.

jingo.title: Jingo
jingo.author: Terry Pratchett
jingo.why: Ankh-Morpork nearly goes to war over a rising island; a sharp, funny Watch story suggested to new readers.

witch elm.title: The Witch Elm
witch elm.author: Tana French
witch elm.why: A man recovering from an attack finds a skull in his family garden; twisty, though a few readers found it slow.

rose field.title: The Rose Field
rose field.author: Philip Pullman
rose field.why: Named only as a disappointing book.

skagboys.title: Skagboys
skagboys.author: Irvine Welsh
skagboys.why: The prequel to Trainspotting follows how its characters fall into heroin; raw, intense and beautifully written.

dragonbone chair.title: The Dragonbone Chair
dragonbone chair.author: Tad Williams
dragonbone chair.why: A kitchen boy is swept into a kingdom's collapse; a classic epic fantasy that inspired many later writers.

raven.title: The Raven
raven.author: Edgar Allan Poe
raven.why: Poe's famous poem of a grieving man and a croaking bird; short, dark and carefully constructed.

childrens bible.title: A Children's Bible
childrens bible.author: Lydia Millet
childrens bible.why: Children watch their adults squander a climate crisis and pandemic; a sharp, thoughtful novel, whatever the title suggests.

empire falls.title: Empire Falls
empire falls.author: Richard Russo
empire falls.why: Life in a declining Maine town; Russo's Pulitzer winner mixes warmth and wry observation.

shell seekers.title: The Shell Seekers
shell seekers.author: Rosamunde Pilcher
shell seekers.why: An elderly woman looks back on her life and family; comforting and richly descriptive.

turtles all the way down.title: Turtles All the Way Down
turtles all the way down.author: John Green
turtles all the way down.why: A teenage girl with anxiety follows a missing-billionaire mystery; a warm YA about mental illness.

rabbits.title: Rabbits
rabbits.author: Terry Miles
rabbits.why: A paranoid thriller about a secret alternate-reality game; ridiculous and confounding in ways its fans love.

hungerstone.title: Hungerstone
hungerstone.author: Kat Dunn
hungerstone.why: A Carmilla retelling in which a vampire helps a woman escape an abusive marriage; sensual gothic horror.

tom jones.title: Tom Jones
tom jones.author: Henry Fielding
tom jones.why: A foundling's bawdy adventures told by an ironic narrator; a delight for some, unreadable for others.

home.title: Home
home.author: Marilynne Robinson
home.why: Comments do not discuss this book.

arcadia.title: Arcadia
arcadia.author: Lauren Groff
arcadia.why: A boy grows up in a 1960s commune; called painfully beautiful, a contemporary Middlemarch.

challenger.title: Challenger
challenger.author: Adam Higginbotham
challenger.why: The Challenger disaster told in gripping detail; readers recommend it alongside other strong narrative non-fiction.

war and peace by leo tolstoy.title: War and Peace
war and peace by leo tolstoy.author: Leo Tolstoy
war and peace by leo tolstoy.why: Napoleonic Russia seen through several families; a monumental novel that readers tackle slowly.

cackle.title: Cackle
cackle.author: Rachel Harrison
cackle.why: A woman moves to a small town where witchcraft is afoot; a cosy, funny horror readers reread.

king leopolds ghost.title: King Leopold's ghost
king leopolds ghost.author: Adam Hochschild
king leopolds ghost.why: The Belgian king's brutal rule of the Congo; readers recommend it, though it is hard to take in.

boyfriend.title: The Boyfriend
boyfriend.author: Freida McFadden
boyfriend.why: Named only as a disappointing book.

swordheart.title: Swordheart
swordheart.author: T. Kingfisher
swordheart.why: A widow and a cursed swordsman bound to her sword make a warm, funny fantasy romance.

book of strange new things.title: The Book of Strange New Things
book of strange new things.author: Michael Faber
book of strange new things.why: A missionary travels to an alien planet while his marriage strains on Earth; weird, moving and praised for its ending.

at home.title: At Home
at home.author: Bill Bryson
at home.why: Bryson tours the rooms of a house, revealing the history of everyday life; readers call it fun and fascinating.

wandering stars.title: Wandering Stars
wandering stars.author: Tommy Orange
wandering stars.why: Tommy Orange follows the descendants of a massacre survivor; readers find it amazing.

venomous lumpsucker.title: Venomous Lumpsucker
venomous lumpsucker.author: Ned Beauman
venomous lumpsucker.why: A darkly funny near-future satire about extinction credits; admired for its ideas.

lightning.title: Lightning
lightning.author: Dean Koontz
lightning.why: A woman is repeatedly saved by a mysterious stranger tied to time travel; readers rank it his best.

herzog.title: Herzog
herzog.author: Saul Bellow
herzog.why: A professor in crisis writes unsent letters to everyone; a brilliant, demanding portrait of a failed genius.

grace of kings.title: The Grace of Kings (The Dandelion Dynasty)
grace of kings.author: Ken Liu
grace of kings.why: Two rebels topple an empire in a silkpunk world; well rated, though some find the pacing heavy.

prozac nation.title: Prozac nation
prozac nation.author: Elizabeth Wurtzel
prozac nation.why: A frank memoir of young adult depression; not for everyone but helpful for readers who relate.

hero of ages.title: The Hero of Ages
hero of ages.author: Brandon Sanderson
hero of ages.why: The final Mistborn book, bringing the trilogy to a satisfying, epic close.

stars in my pocket like grains of sand.title: Stars in my pocket like grains of sand
stars in my pocket like grains of sand.author: Samuel R. Delany
stars in my pocket like grains of sand.why: Delany's galactic love story across cultures and unusual sexuality; difficult but rewarding.

flow my tears the policeman said.title: Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said
flow my tears the policeman said.author: Philip K. Dick
flow my tears the policeman said.why: A TV star wakes in a world where he does not exist; a paranoid Dick classic.

house of the scorpion.title: The House of the Scorpion
house of the scorpion.author: Nancy Farmer
house of the scorpion.why: A clone raised in a drug lord's household fights to be treated as human; a school favourite people remember.

homeseeking.title: Homeseeking
homeseeking.author: Karissa Chen
homeseeking.why: A Chinese couple separated by war across decades; recommended to fans of Pachinko.
